newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends easy, gilts up in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends easy, gilts up in brisk trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday at 4.0-4.25 percent, down from opening quotes of 5.0-5.5 percent on good funds supply, dealers said.
They said strong inflows from maturing securities and interest payments will keep liquidity easy and call money rates in a tight range over the next two weeks.
"About 17 billion rupees from 14-day treasury bills came in on Saturday and more funds will come in this week," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
SBI Capital Markets said in a debt market report that inflows from redemptions of securities and interest payments will be more than 56 billion rupees in the coming fortnight.
Dealers said prices of government securities rose in brisk trade but fell slightly in late trade on rumours the government will announce a bond issue shortly.

"Prices rose in the morning and were generally up through the day," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "But they fell marginally in the afternoon on market reports the government is coming out with a bond issue soon."
Dealers said most of Monday's trade was in short- and medium-term securities.

Among actively traded stocks, the 13.50 percent 1998 stock traded on Monday at 103.5 rupees against 103.31 on Saturday. The 12.59 percent 2004 traded at 101.20 against 100.9, the 13.40 percent 1998 rose to 105.56 from 105.4 and the 13.80 percent 2002 rose to 106.49 from 106.36, dealers said.
Treasury bills auctioned on July 4 at 6.98 percent was traded at 6.7 percent in the secondary market, dealers said.
